subject: Mutual Action Track: implementation playbook & training sprint for Lyra Health
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyrahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@lyrahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for production rollout and MAP

Vanessa — thanks again for the overview today. Procurement has a couple of timeline constraints but we want to lock the technical milestones so we can align SOW sign-off. High level asks from Lyra:

- A short canary that demonstrates failure isolation and automatic fallback.
- A training plan for the clinical operations team (2 sessions + on-demand recordings).
- Clear migration windows that avoid peak hours (we’re east-coast heavy).

I attached the Lyra internal deployment blackout windows and our compliance checklist. Can you confirm the migration duration estimate and who from Redwood will own the runbook on go-live day?

— Liam

Attachment: lyra_blackout_windows_2027.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyrahealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@lyrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps for production rollout and MAP

Liam — great to have that context. I’ve pulled together an initial mutual action track (attached) that embeds the post-sign implementation sequence, canary criteria, migration windows, and the training sprint. Highlights below: 

- Canary: 48-hour rolling canary on a subset of traffic (5% sessions) with automatic fallback to baseline model variant; success criteria = <1% error spike, latencies within 2x baseline.
- Migration: typical cutover is planned for a 3-hour maintenance window starting 22:00 ET; full rollback plan included.
- Training: two live sessions (40-60 min) plus 6 on-demand videos; ops playbook and runbook owners listed.
- Acceptance: post-canary evaluation plan with a 72-hour quality review tied to your eval prompts.

I’ll assign owners in the spreadsheet and propose concrete dates after we confirm your preferred week. Karthik is briefed to lead the canary execution; Stephanie will own training delivery coordination.

Attached: RDW_LYRA_MAP_v1.2.xlsx; deployment_diagram.png

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Strategic Accounts Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0183

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyrahealth.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mutual Action Track: implementation playbook & training sprint for Lyra Health

Looping in the technical owners — quick notes on canary execution and migration duration estimates: 

- Canary runbook: we will use traffic routing policy to send 5% of calls to the canary variant and keep prefix/KV cache warming for 24 hours prior. KVs will be seeded from a prewarm task to limit cold-start tail latency.
- Observability: Redwood Console route will expose token-level latency and error budgets; we’ll generate an automatic regression alert if latency P95 > 2x baseline or error rate > 1%.
- Estimated migration: 3-hour window for cutover; 30-45 minutes for canary validation, 10–15 minute promotion, remaining time for verification and stakeholder signoff.

I’ve attached a short PDF with the proposed rollback commands and monitoring checks. I recommend running the canary in the east region first to match Lyra traffic.

Attachment: canary_rollout_windows.pdf

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@lyrahealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyrahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyrahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Track: implementation playbook & training sprint for Lyra Health

Thanks — that layout looks good. A couple clarifications from our side: 

1) Can you confirm who will be the primary contact on go-live day for incident escalation? (we prefer a single point for speed)
2) Training: can the second live session be scheduled a week after go-live for ops to cover issues uncovered during the canary?
3) Procurement needs the SOW milestone list (not just the MAP) to match billing triggers. Can you attach that?

We can target week of June 7 for the canary if that works for Redwood.

— Aisha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha.patel@lyrahealth.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@lyrahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@lyrahealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 13:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Track: implementation playbook & training sprint for Lyra Health

Aisha — answers inline: 

1) Primary escalation contact: Karthik Iyer (karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com) — reachable by phone and Slack; escalation matrix included in the MAP.
2) Yes — second live training scheduled for +7 days post-promote to capture canary learnings. Stephanie will draft the session agenda with QA.
3) SOW milestone list: attached as a one-page milestone excerpt and I’ll push the full SOW PDF to the DocuSign link for signatures. Billing milestones will map to: (a) contract execution, (b) canary completion and acceptance, (c) production promote.

Proposed timeline: 
- 2027-06-07: Prewarm and low-traffic canary (east region)
- 2027-06-08: 48-hr extended validation window
- 2027-06-15: Production promote (subject to acceptance)

Please confirm the dates and I’ll lock them in the MAP.

Thanks,
Vanessa
